I would cancel it months back, but you guys were absolutely awesome with feedback, so I could not do it. If you're a playtest player, is reading this and would like to keep testing the game, I beg you, hit me at leonardo@zanardiliza.com! I would like to send something to you.

If for some reason you see any issue, or have any funny ideas, suggestion, or just want to chat, please hit me here on Steam or on our discord at:
https://discord.gg/xKDbh66ZW9

notes.title: Patch notes for November 7
notes.content:
I was hyped by some FPS gain in November 1, so I've silently published a patch with it. That patch had the following updates:
-changed how spider bot legs works
-level load times significantly improved
-changed enemy IK - improved performance

Today, we're uploading a patch with the following changes:
-Improved some performance tasks
-Improved how Level Generation works - Load times significantly improved
-Crosshair now hides when using the pc
-Fixed overlap on Input Settings Screen
-Thick/Thin crosshair was inverted, fixed
-Added new level to EP 3. It's kinda blocky, lots of assets and things to do, very W.I.P

That's all for this patch.

I would like to take some time to talk more about the future of FDP's development.

At the beggining, 4 different episodes were expected, episodes that could be playied alone, where the game could reach it's finale after beating Episode 4. Lots of things happened since, and I've decided to make some changes on the project as a whole.
For start, I'm cutting one episode, making the game 3 episodes lengthy, and removing the option to play the episodes separately. They would be playied in a row - in a single play, and the game challenege would escalate on this 3 episodes run.
I thought a lot about the matter, and I've made ammends with it because of some key points:
- I want to work more on the city content. Make new stores, new secret things, new ways of enemy showing up on the streets.
- Also want to work more on the current game levels. Every one of the existing levels. They need more depth, secret things, content, replayability.
- More importantly - the game will not finish after finishing the last episode. There's new content that will be added for another half of the game, kinda spoiler but it may be showed soon (maybe December).

I want like to apologize for the mess that some things are - Episode 2 and 3 levels really needs more work, and I'm rushing to shape everything ASAP. I'm also almost finishing the base parts of all levels, so I may focus on developing everything better later.
I want also to thank everyone for the patience and support.

notes.title: Patch notes for May 30
notes.content:
This one took a little more time, on a fundamental ingame change that I needed to approach.

But why? Two things: first, since the game does not lock you on finding colored keys or activating things, I was looking into ways of giving meaning to the game combat, to... you know, avoid the game being an entire speedrun only thing.
Another issue was the Rogue-Lite elements. Until now, the way to save things on your house stash was to drop any weapon-or-item on a mailbox, then this item would be saved on your cabin/hub. I personally like when there's not-so-obvious design ideas on game (Dog Duty is totally based on that) but... I think that the mail box alone was not doing it's job, and also, imposing some limitations.

So... how to solve those 2 questions? Well... since Liza LOVES to browse stuff on e-shops (I dont see reason on that, but that's her thing) I'm changing the game system to work with currency, and adding some e-shops on the cabin's computer. So now.... you may win currency by killing enemies, and you may use it to buy permanent upgrades, house decor, and weapons, on the confort of your basement's computer.

But beware, dying ingame makes you lose 95% of your currency - you will be able to keep it by:
a - depositing the value on mailboxes
b - ending the episode

What do you think? That makes sense?
Also, on this patch, other things:
-Changed the animations a little when the enemies are walking and shooting.
-Tweaked ingame code a bit, maybe the game will perform better, load faster too.
-Music volume now responds right for ingame-soundtrack
-Your in-hand weapon will move a little when moving the camera
-Miscs/etc

notes.title: We need you. A lot.
notes.content:
When developing something new, we usually bumb into local gaming events and show our thing. You know, to stalk the player, watching it's movements, to get what goes right, where it's enjoyable, or when the thing is so shitty that the player get out to do something better.
But heck... we're on quarantine. No events in sight.

So we need you. A lot.

We cant stalk you online so... we're in dire need of human feedback. This game is some kind of Retro FPS with some sort of random content, with a light dose of survival elements, with lot's of odd content.
It works? Makes sense? Is it fun?

So... if you have played it, please, let us know how was your experience. Feel free to reach us anywhere, here on Steam, on leonardo@zanardiliza.com, well, anywhere.
Thank you a lot for joying this game,
Leonardo Zimbres, AKA Zanardi.
